newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, Indonesia open telephone cable link.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Indonesia open telephone cable link.

text.p: Australia and Indonesia opened the Jasuraus telephone cable network linking the two countries at ceremonies held in Sydney and Jakarta on Monday that would provide faster communication access between the two nations.

The A$160 million Jasuraus cable was a cooperative venture between Australian telecom groups Telstra Corp and Optus Communications Pty Ltd and Indonesian carrier PT Indonesian Satellite Corp (Indosat).
Telstra chief operating officer Frank Blount said at the Sydney launch that the new cable has the capacity to facilitate 60,000 telephone conversations simultaneously.

Optus chief operating officer Ziggy Switkowski said the 2,800 km cable would give Australian organisations the access they need to technology and voice data services in Australia and Asia into the next century.

Indonesian Secretary General of Telecommunications, Post and Tourism Jonathan Parapak said via a vidoe link from Jakarta that the Jasuraus cable could lead to growth in trade and tourism between the two countries.
The Jasuraus cable is part of the Asia Pacific Cable Network that links Japan, South Korea, Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia and Australia.
